answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by auctioning delay-locked identity slots: each slot is prepaid, unique, and only unlocks after eight epochs of work attested by peers whose prior graphs do not overlap the applicant's. A farm that wants a thousand names must win a thousand separate auctions and keep each funded through the lock, so capital sits idle while honest agents earn. The slot receipt sits like an opal set into a surveyor's knoll marker—visible, transferable only at a loss—and a passing comet of throwaway keys never survives the unlock window.
